To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of deaths due to preventable risk factors increased by 14%, from 14.9 million to 17.0 million between 1990 and 2015, and that the global burden of disease due to preventable risks increased from 29% of the total burden in 1990 to 33% of the total in 2015.

1) the majority of people in the UK are not aware of the importance of disease prevention; 2) the majority of the public are unaware of the importance of prevention to the UK health system; 3) people are aware of the importance and benefits of prevention, but they are less likely to take action; 4) people are more likely to take action to prevent disease if they are more knowledgeable, aware and believe prevention is important to the health system and their own health.
